original_question: Let n be a positive integer, and let A1, ..., An be self-adjoint real n x n matrices with spectral norms bounded by 1 (that is, ||Ai|| <= 1 for every i). Does there exist a universal constant C > 0 such that one can always choose signs epsilon1, ..., epsilonn in {+1, -1} so that the operator norm of the signed sum is bounded by C*sqrt(n): ||sum_{i=1}^n epsiloni Ai|| <= C*sqrt(n)?
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation: it quantifies over every positive integer n, uses exactly n self-adjoint real n×n matrices A1,...,An, assumes ||Ai|| <= 1 for each i, asks for a universal constant C, and asks for a signing by epsilons in {+1,-1} that makes the signed sum have norm O(sqrt(n)). ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
missing_details: To match the paper verbatim, say explicitly that the norm in both the hypothesis and conclusion is the spectral norm. The paper names this norm right in the statement. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))

The paper writes the claim in minimization form, namely min_{epsilon in {±1}^n} ||sum_{i=1}^n epsilon_i Ai|| <= C sqrt(n), rather than only as an existential choice of signs. This is mathematically equivalent but is the official formulation used there. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
refined_question: Conjecture (Matrix Spencer). Does there exist a positive universal constant C such that, for every positive integer n and every choice of n self-adjoint real n×n matrices A1,...,An satisfying ||Ai|| <= 1 for all i in [n], where ||·|| denotes the spectral norm, one has min_{epsilon in {±1}^n} ||sum_{i=1}^n epsilon_i Ai|| <= C sqrt(n)? ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting exactly the Matrix Spencer conjecture stated in Entry 1. The surrounding context on the same page makes clear that this is being presented as the noncommutative analogue of Spencer's vector discrepancy theorem, that the noncommutative Khintchine inequality only gives the desired bound up to an extra sqrt(log n) factor, and that the paper keeps the formulation in the real self-adjoint n-matrices / n×n-matrices / spectral-norm setting. Those remarks support keeping the question narrowly in that form rather than broadening it to other dimensions, fields, or norms. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
